title: Version Control and Collaboration
learning_outcomes: Describe when version control and collaboration is useful and what problem it does not solve.
Evaluate a small example against its stated constraints, standard version and implementation assumptions.
Select a test or tool that can provide evidence of correctness without treating one successful run as proof.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text:
Professional C++ work requires reproducible builds, diagnostics, tests, dependency hygiene, secure boundaries and measurement. A passing build alone is not proof of correctness.

Version Control and Collaboration focuses on the decisions and observable behavior named by the subtopics below. The aim is to explain the rule, predict what a small program should do, and then confirm the result with a focused check.

Use compiler warnings, repeatable tests, static analysis and sanitizers as complementary signals; keep tool configuration under version control.

content_blocks.title: Minimal example: Version Control and Collaboration
content_blocks.run_instructions: Save as `example.cpp`. Compile using `g++ -std=c++20 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic example.cpp -o example; then run ./example (Windows: .\example.exe).` The CodeLeaf page shows reference output only; it does not execute C++ learner code.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the example, rebuild with the same standard and warning flags, and rerun the same input. If the example is nondeterministic or depends on platform support, record that constraint instead of expecting byte-for-byte identical output.
content_blocks.limitations: The built-in CodeLeaf page does not execute C++ in a sandbox. Compile local teaching examples only; arbitrary learner code requires a separately deployed isolated runner with CPU, memory, process, filesystem and network limits.

content_blocks.title: Guided practice
content_blocks.text: Before changing the example, predict the output and name the rule that produces it. Then modify one line to demonstrate git fundamentals, and add a test for one boundary or failure scenario. Keep the experiment small enough that another learner can reproduce it.

content_blocks.title: Version, safety and portability note
content_blocks.text: This topic may depend on newer C++ language or library support; this example uses a C++20-compatible illustration. Feature support varies by compiler version and standard-library implementation. Check the references and prefer explicit diagnostics to assumptions.

content.task: Create a small, independent example that demonstrates version control and collaboration. Predict the result before compiling, write down a precondition, and test one ordinary case plus one boundary or failure case.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example builds under a documented standard mode with warnings enabled.
The predicted and observed result are recorded; deviations are explained.
At least one boundary, invalid-input, lifetime or portability assumption is tested or documented.
hints: Start with the smallest example that demonstrates git fundamentals.
Trace the relevant values and state the expected output before running the program.
Check the standard/compiler reference and add an edge case instead of relying only on the happy path.
summary: Version Control and Collaboration is about a concrete language rule or engineering decision, not only terminology.
Keep the important preconditions and trade-offs visible when applying version control and collaboration.
Use explicit build settings and focused tests to support the claim that the example behaves as expected.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming one successful example proves every case.
common_mistakes.why: It may miss an invalid input, boundary, error path or implementation difference.
common_mistakes.fix: Write down the preconditions and test at least one ordinary case plus an edge or failure case.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a language feature without checking its requirements.
common_mistakes.why: The code may depend on a standard version, an object lifetime or an API precondition.
common_mistakes.fix: Use the explicit standard mode and verify the relevant rule and compiler/library support.

common_mistakes.problem: Ignoring compiler diagnostics or simplifying away ownership and error behavior.
common_mistakes.why: Warnings and explicit contracts often expose a defect before it becomes a runtime problem.
common_mistakes.fix: Compile with warnings, keep the smallest reproducible sample and state what happens when an operation fails.
